supported_claims.text: The early graph for 事 is described as a hand holding an object, and the related graphs 史、吏、事、使 were initially one graph before later differentiation. The held object has been identified variously as a flag, document container, brush, or implement; none is established.

Bronze-inscription examples use 事 for duty or office, events, and commanding or serving. Other cited early-text and manuscript examples attest matters, events, undertaking, and serving. These support multiple uses, not a fully ordered semantic history.

The received Shuowen account glosses 事 as office or duty and analyzes it as 从史，之省聲, with 史 as a meaning element and abbreviated 之 as a sound element. This is a later lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the early graph's formation.

The dossier lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen form categories, and supplies a modern redraw of a received Shuowen-style seal form. These records do not date an individual earliest specimen.

disagreements.text: The paleographic account describes the early graph as a hand holding an unidentified object, with 史、吏、事、使 differentiating from a shared graph; the Shuowen account instead analyzes 事 through 史 plus abbreviated 之 as phonetic. The dossier does not resolve whether that later component analysis applies to the ancient graph.

The held object has competing proposed identifications, including a flag, bamboo-document container, writing brush, divination or hunting implement. The evidence does not establish which object was depicted.

limitations.text: The exact earliest attested instance and archaeological date of 事 are not established by the cited form categories or examples.
The object's name and pronunciation are not established, so a claim that 事 was borrowed from the name of the depicted object cannot be supported here.
The cited examples attest several uses but do not establish a complete chronology or a single linear semantic development among them.

Modern or reconstructed reading pairs for 事 and 史 in local data do not independently prove that 史 supplied the ancient graph's pronunciation; the local rows were not externally verified in the research described.
